research_question: How do mycorrhizal fungi connect with plant roots, and what evidence supports claims about resource transfer or communication between trees?

sources.title: The Wood Wide Web: myth or reality?
notes: Popular 'wood wide web' claims have been debated for overstatement.
Evidence of a network or transfer does not by itself prove intentional cooperation.
Field significance and prevalence require careful evaluation.

sources.title: Mycorrhizal fungi and plant nutrition
notes: Mycorrhizal fungi can help plants acquire nutrients and water.
Plant-fungus outcomes depend on species and environmental conditions.

sources.title: Common mycorrhizal networks: a review
notes: Mycorrhizal associations can connect plant roots via fungal hyphae.
Research examines transfer pathways, network prevalence, and ecological outcomes.
Laboratory results require careful interpretation before generalization to forests.

sources.title: The hidden world of the soil
notes: Soil contains diverse fungi and organisms involved in plant ecology.
Below-ground biodiversity contributes to forest function.

sources.title: Do trees communicate through fungal networks?
notes: The 'wood wide web' phrase popularizes underground fungal connections.
Popular descriptions should be separated from the limits of scientific evidence.
